date-fns.message: Import date-fns by module path instead: date-fns/isValid. A bare specifier pulls the whole 245-export index into the module graph; when the lambdas resolved it from the dependencies layer that cost 508 ms of cold start against 8 ms for one module (KOE-6). Bundling (KOE-1330) now tree-shakes it away for the lambdas, but the module path stays the convention -- the frontend build has not been measured.

patterns.message: Frontend and shared code must not import from src/lambda. Move the shared code to src/lib or src/types instead; see src/lib/README.md.
Frontend and shared code must not depend on the AWS SDK. Mirror the needed shape in src/types instead (see EmailTemplateContent in src/types/Email.ts).

A calendar day is a DayKey, and its conversions live in src/lib/day.ts: dayOf, dayStart, dayEnd, addDays, daysBetween, eachDay, shiftDays (KOE-1545). date-fns calendar functions (isSameDay, startOfDay, addDays, nextSaturday, subWeeks, ...) read the day in the machine's zone, and format and parseISO do the same with day tokens and day keys: format a moment with formatDate (src/i18n/dates.ts), read a day key with dayStart after isDayKey. Only instant functions are allowed here (isValid, isAfter, differenceInMinutes, formatDistanceToNowStrict, lightFormat of a build time, ...). A line that must keep a calendar call carries a biome-ignore with the reason and the issue that moves it.
